q: My wife is currently shopping for Doulas to help us with our incoming twins and it is causing some... discussions. I cannot fathom paying $70/hour (~$3200 minimum contract) for someone to watch our kids while we are both off work.
cx: Father of one, twins on the way; the couple disagree about hiring help.

q: I think social media, some of it thinly veiled ads for doulas, is making her think if we are tired we are going to suffocate the baby in our sleep or run the car into a tree from exhaustion.
cx: Why he thinks his wife wants a doula.
r: safe sleep and road-safety fears named (no incident)

q: my wife said we'd need to account for about "thirty-two" for the doula, and I was like "oh hourly? that's not bad for a 'treat-yo-self' every few days"... and she was like no thirty-two hundred minimum, $65/hr (i rounded up lol).
cx: How he learned the doula price.

q: the doulas we've contacted (well, she's contacted) have an obligation to imply scarcity and need a contract months ahead.
cx: His view of how doulas sell.

q: I think I'm now focusing on just having a doula on standby for ad-hoc visits but am very apprehensive to drop $3k on a *maybe*
cx: His compromise after replies.

q: This is such as hard decision because the minimum contract periods. For example, say I'm 3 nights into my doula service and I'm feeling disconnected from my newborns, I can't just cancel on the contract. Similarly, if I don't get someone under contract and my wife is pissed at me because everyone's booked and we look like night of the living dead.
cx: Why the minimum contract makes the decision hard.

q: You know... I think I am being kind of selfish here... she complained about lack of sleep but I didn't really dig into it with her other than that point.
cx: Reply to a commenter asking if his wife enjoyed the first baby as he did.

q: We’re expecting twins towards the end of October (super excited), but I am terrified I will not have the energy to handle all 3 kids, I am also terrified that I’ll be too tired to do anything and have everything fall on my fiancés back.
cx: Father always tired despite ten hours of sleep.

q: I'm naturally a side sleeper anyway, and I have found my yoga bolster works just fine between my legs as I've been getting bigger. What would a pregnancy pillow do for me that my bolster doesn't?
cx: Asks whether to buy a pregnancy pillow.

q: Hi! I’m working with a sleep consultant as I have a 10 month old. We start the plan today/ tonight for sleep training.
cx: Baby wakes after 4-5 hours and won't resettle; husband works nights.

q: I should have done sleep training to begin with but I’m exhausted. My husband works shift work as well so does a lot of nights.
cx: Why she hired a sleep consultant.

q: I haven’t been sleeping for months. I’ve had horrible insomnia. And yes - I have the pillow, I’ve done the unisom, the magnesium, melatonin, and Benadryl. It doesn’t work.
cx: 37 weeks pregnant.

q: Ive been mindful to get steps in every day to physically prep my body for sleep. My doctor told me to stop taking naps. lol. I switch from my bed to the couch most nights at this point.
cx: What she does and what her doctor said.

q: I’m still awake right now “from yesterday”. I want to cry. This is as bad as it’s gotten but I’m just so frustrated that I’ve been left to deal with this on my own for months and now I’m just not falling asleep.
cx: Three nights this week without falling asleep at all.

q: On top of that, my inability to sleep has started to affect my husband’s ability to get a good night rest and he’s been miserable at work, impatient
cx: Her insomnia spreading to her husband.

q: This is a good idea but I have a high deductible insurance. I’m not even sure my hospital would allow that.
cx: Reply to a suggestion for medical help with sleep.

q:
I’m 27wk 3days and have insane hip and leg paid at night. I’ve tried everything I feel like and I can’t sleep this is awful. 

I recently started using a pregnancy pillow but I don’t feel like it working at all.
cx: Night hip pain despite a new pillow.

q: My husband works in healthcare with a 12 hour night shift schedule 6 pm - 6 am. Our plan for baby is for him to be on night shift during his paternity leave and I’ll take day shifts, and we’re both happy with this plan.
cx: Planning the newborn nights before birth.

q: I’ll basically be “on” for 72 hours as he works 3 or 4 days in a row. […] We are not in a position to hire a night nanny, and family help is not a trustworthy option for a variety of reasons.
cx: What happens when he returns to night shifts at six weeks.

q: I bought Precious Little Sleep and attempted to SLIP with nursing to sleep.
cx: Exclusively breastfed 7.5-month-old who nursed to sleep.

q: (Ps: we also tried “gentle sleep training” and paid $$$$ for a sleep coach but it did nothing. This thread is worth more money than any sleep coach.)
cx: Footnote to her success post.

q: However, I’m so glad we committed to making a change and have slept better the last 2 nights than I have since she was born.
cx: Night four of sleep training; baby slept 11.5 hours on night three.

q: I also got sucked into Instagram influencers talking about cosleeping and felt guilty for starting to feel like this wasn’t a sustainable lifestyle for us. The sleep deprivation was really starting to destroy me and I felt at the end of my rope.
cx: Before sleep training.

q: I hired someone to give baby bottles of breastmilk at night so I could at least sleep 4 hour blocks. I would breastfeed and pump during the day and then just pump at night to keep up with supply. This worked for a little while but I would still wake up whenever my baby cried (he is very impatient and does not like to wait for the bottle to be warmed up) and most times I have trouble falling back to sleep. I have always been a terrible sleeper.
cx: Fourteen weeks; returning next week to a stressful job.
r: mental health (hire followed anxiety and depression)

q: Thinking about going back to this place next week and not being able to pump enough milk for my baby is ALREADY making me not produce enough milk so currently I can't even keep up with the night bottles he needs so I can sleep my 4 hour blocks.
cx: Why her paid night help is ending.

q:
Have paid for the help of a very good sleep consultant as I prefer someone to tell me exactly what to do.

Sleep deprivation has probably been one of the hardest things I’ve had to deal with at the level I’ve had it. I think I could handle anything with a bit of sleep now.
cx: Sleep training starts at four months.

q: We have been paying for overnight doula support 2-3x a week to help us not get so burned out and were going to be able to continue with 1-2x a week after I go back to work. When we have no doula, I get 2-3 hours of sleep max (EBF, also pumping) and with a doula, I get 5-6 hours minimum.
cx: Reflux baby, 3.5 months; she returns to work in a month.

q:
A) hire a full time nanny, M-F 9am-6pm for $1,000 a week AND discontinue all overnight doula support

Or

B) use traditional daycare for $250-350 a week AND continue 2 nights doula support for $700 a week
cx: Their two options after a $500-a-week childminder fell through.

q: We agreed upon $500/week, we would provide all equipment/toys/food/gear including a car seat
cx: The neighbourhood childcare deal that fell through.

q: We went away to visit family for 10 days and without the overnight help, averaged 2 hours of sleep per night. It was torture.
cx: What nights look like without the doula.

q: This schedule has made the idea of shift work difficult because we don't really have enough overlapping time to break it up well especially because I'm breastfeeding, which isn't something we are willing to alter.
cx: Both commute an hour; husband leaves at 6am.

q: Thank you, that's the root of the conflict. Sleep deprivation vs flexible, dedicated care for a higher needs baby.
cx: Summing up the nanny-or-doula choice.

q:
I go to bed cold, bundled up under blankets, and wake up soaked!

Any tips on how to reduce this? I’m thinking of buying a cooling comforter.
cx: Five weeks pregnant with night sweats.

q: Our baby has a really solid sleep routine now because we spent 5 months in sleep deprived hell, so we have got him to a great, consistent place through the use of a sleep consultant.
cx: Parent of a 9.5-month-old; in-laws skip naps.

q: Would highly recommend, she has got us back on track multiple times and tackled lots of issues like sleep associations, dummy’s, move to cots and own room, etc etc
cx: Recommending her sleep consultant to a commenter.
